heading: INT. HYPERBARIC CLINIC - CHAMBER ROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. HYPERBARIC CLINIC - CHAMBER ROOM - DAY
A converted cannery on a grey harbor.
Inside, a steel hyperbaric chamber the size of a school bus squats on the old conveyor floor, its portholes fogged, its rivets painted a cheerful hospital blue.
Pipes bundle along the ceiling like the ribs of something sleeping.
Gulls scream beyond the high windows.
The room hums with compressors and the faint metronome tick of a pressure gauge.
DR. SIGRID LUND (50s, silver braid, reading glasses pushed into her hair) stands at the control console.
She moves with unhurried care, as though the machine might wake if she is careless.
A mug of tea sits cooling beside the dials.
NURSE TEMBO ADEYEMI (30s, scrubs the color of lichen, a pencil through her bun) checks a chart on a clipboard.
She hums something.
She is the only one who hums.
BARRY QUILL (40s, technician, oil on his knuckles, a lanyard of tiny brass keys) taps a gauge with one finger and frowns.
He taps it again, softer.
Through the nearest porthole: ARAM VOSKANIAN (70s), reclined on a padded gurney inside the chamber, a clear hood over his white hair.
He lifts a hand to the glass, as if to wave at a passing train.
His daughter LENKA VOSKANIAN (40s, tailored coat, phone clutched like a rosary) sits beside the porthole in the antechamber.
He's at two atmospheres. Pulse is steady. He asked if we have any radio in there.
units.name: TEMBO

units.text: Tell him no. The static makes the oxygen worse.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: I told him that. He said he doesn't mind static if it's honest.
units.name: TEMBO

units.text: Sigrid almost laughs.
She sips the tea.
It is cold.
She sips anyway.
How long?
units.name: LENKA

units.text: Ninety minutes. We run the whole protocol. He is doing wonderfully.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: He hasn't done anything wonderfully since my mother died.
units.name: LENKA

units.text: Sigrid says nothing.
Tembo glances up from the chart, then away.
Come on, old girl. Hold the line.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: The needle trembles and holds.
Barry exhales.
He wipes his hands on a rag.
In the chamber, Aram closes his eyes.
Beneath the hood, his lips move.
He may be praying.
He may be singing.
Lenka watches him and presses her palm flat against the glass.
He's lucky to have you.
units.name: TEMBO

units.text: He doesn't know I'm here.
units.name: LENKA

units.text: He knows.
units.name: TEMBO

units.text: The compressor cycles.
A long breath of air rushes through the pipes.
Everyone in the room unconsciously matches it, inhaling and holding.
Then the gauge ticks.
Once.
Twice.
Barry stops breathing.
Doctor.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: I see it.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: That's not the chamber. That's the supply line.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: I said I see it, Barry.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: She sets down the mug.
Her hand does not shake.
Her eyes do not leave the needle.
A speaker crackles on the wall.
DR. IMAI (V.O.) speaks from the control room upstairs, voice thin and tired.
Lund, the oxygen reservoir is reading low. Do you copy?
units.name: DR. IMAI

units.text: Copy, Imai. We're checking.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: Check faster.
units.name: DR. IMAI

units.text: Sigrid releases a valve.
Tembo steps in to help without being asked.
They work side by side, silent, practiced, their sleeves brushing.
What's happening?
units.name: LENKA

units.text: ^Nothing to worry about.
units.name: TEMBO

units.text: Routine adjustment.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: They say it at the same instant, to the same person, with the same smile.
Lenka looks from one face to the other.
She doesn't believe either.
In the chamber, Aram opens his eyes.
He sees the three of them moving fast beyond the glass.
He smiles gently, as if he already knows.
The gauge climbs.
Barry kneels, finds the leaking coupling, and clamps it with bare hands.
Steam hisses against his palms.
He does not let go.
Got it. Got it. Hold on.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: His voice cracks.
Sigrid turns the main valve.
The hiss stops.
The needle steadies.
Silence.
Then, slowly, gulls again.
Tembo rests her forehead against the cold steel of the console.
Sigrid lays a hand on her shoulder.
Neither moves.
Barry unclamps his burned hands, stares at them, laughs once, helplessly.
Is he all right?
units.name: LENKA

units.text: Sigrid walks to the porthole.
Aram raises one thumb, slow, deliberate.
He's perfect.
units.name: SIGRID

units.text: Lenka sinks into the chair, finally letting the phone drop to her lap.
It buzzes.
Nobody reaches for it.
The tea, forgotten, tips off the console and shatters on the cannery floor.
